How ohms law is calculated

Solve one unknown in Ohm’s law using any two of voltage, current, and resistance, then report power. Inputs must describe the same circuit condition; the equations model ideal lumped electrical behavior and do not cover nonlinear components or transient effects. 12 V across 6 Ω gives 2 A and 24 W. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. The calculator checks consistency and reports a mismatch rather than choosing one value arbitrarily. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

V = I × R; P = V × I
A worked example

12 V across 6 Ω gives 2 A and 24 W.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

What if I enter all three values?

The calculator checks consistency and reports a mismatch rather than choosing one value arbitrarily.

Does Ohm’s law apply to every component?

Only to components behaving ohmically over the relevant operating range.
